item.title: This week in science: Archaeology fakes, hurricanes and lizards, and heat health effects
item.description: NPR's Regina Barber and Nate Rott talk about a new way to spot archaeological fakes, how hurricanes may have influenced lizard evolution and the health effects of extreme heat.

item.title: Scientists study how the brain of a fish filters out signals
item.description: The elephantnose fish is native to Africa and a darling of neuroscientists, for its specialized cerebellum-like brain. Scientists have mapped the neurons in a part of the brain that senses electrical signals in detail, and found that how it filters out electrical noise is more complex than they thought.

item.title: NPR spent 2 years tracking deaths from heat. We found a staggering hidden toll
item.description: An NPR investigation found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat much more often than official counts show. We explore the reasons why — and how lives can be saved.

item.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
item.description: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.
